tip: известна (izvestna = is known) puts the person who knows in the dative: мне (mne = to me), literally the problem is known to me.
Here с (s = with) takes the genitive, not the instrumental: с чашки (s chashki = with a cup), meaning starting from.
даётся (dayotsya = comes easily) puts the person in the dative: ей (yey = to her); математика (matematika = maths) stays the subject.
интересуется (interesuyetsya = is interested) takes the instrumental: русской историей (russkoy istoriyey = in Russian history).
смеются (smeyutsya = they laugh) keeps the -ся ending; the verb смеяться (smeyatsya) has no form without it.
Past tense agrees with the subject's gender. ела (yela = ate) ends in -ла for a female speaker; a man would say ел (yel).
без (bez = without) takes the genitive: друзей (druzey = of friends) from друзья (druzya).
The person you write to goes in the dative: другу (drugu = to a friend) from друг (drug).
над (nad = over) takes the instrumental: городом (gorodom = over the city) from город (gorod).
The verb пользуется (polzuetsya = uses) takes the instrumental with no preposition: компьютером (kompyuterom = computer).
вместо (vmesto = instead of) takes the genitive: сахара (sakhara = of sugar) from сахар (sakhar).
After numbers, 'people' uses the count form человек: шесть человек (shest chelavek = six people), not человеков (chelavekov).
The instrumental alone means 'with a tool': карандашом (karandashom = with a pencil), no preposition needed.
кажется (kazhetsya = it seems) marks the person with the dative: мне (mne = to me) gives 'it seems to me'.
привыкаю (privykayu = getting used to) takes к plus the dative: к новому городу (k novomu gorodu = to the new city).
стал (stal = became) puts the new role in the instrumental: чемпионом (chempionom = champion).
Imperfective future is будет (budet = will) plus the infinitive: будет читать (budet chitat = will be reading).
старше (starshe = older) is the comparative; add чем (chem = than) to name what you compare with.
за город (za gorod = out of town) uses за plus accusative for motion; за городом (za gorodom) would mean staying there.
Russian gives a name with меня зовут (menya zavut = literally 'they call me'), using the accusative меня.
пока (paka = while) pairs with imperfective past for two ongoing actions: ждал (zhdal = was waiting).
The reflexive ending -ся (-sya) on оборачивается (abarachivayetsya = turns) points the action back at the subject.
For ‘about’ use о (o): позаботься о себе (pazabotsya o sebe = take care of yourself), об (ob) before a vowel.
The verb боюсь (bayus = I fear) takes its object in the genitive: боюсь темноты (bayus temnaty = afraid of the dark), not the accusative.
Imperfective future is будет (budet = will be) plus an unchanged infinitive: будет готовить (budet gatovit = will cook).
Possession uses the genitive after the noun: голос певца (golos pevtsa = the singer's voice), literally voice of-the-singer.
готовиться к (gatovitsya k = to prepare for) takes the dative: готовились к отъезду (gatovilis k atyezdu = we prepared for departure).
The position word перед (pered = before, in front of) takes the instrumental: перед экзаменом (pered ekzamenom = before the exam).
у (u = by, near) plus the genitive marks location: у окна (u akna = by the window), from окно (akno = window).
A single perfective verb states the future: прочитаю (prachitayu = I will read and finish), no будет (budet) needed.
